report.verdict: Cobalt Pay is a management step beyond the work your resume shows. Your payouts and ledger work is strong, but I can't see direct-report management, hiring or performance reviews.
write_up: Cobalt Pay wants an engineering manager, while your resume presents you as a senior backend engineer. Your payouts, ledger and reliability work fit the platform well; the management experience the role asks for isn't shown.

Your resume is strong for senior backend roles because it connects technical decisions to results. The balance API line is a model: it names the change, the approach and the before-and-after latency. The progression from insurance to freight technology to payments is easy to follow.

For Cobalt Pay, start with any management or team-direction work you've actually done but haven't included. Keep the payments results prominent. For senior backend applications, the resume itself is unlikely to be the thing holding you back; competition for the role and a referral can also matter.

cards.where: Senior Software Engineer, Payments Platform, line 3
cards.line: Cut p99 latency on the balance API from 900 ms to 140 ms by moving reads to a Kafka-fed cache
cards.cannot_tell: Keep this as a model. A recruiter can see both the performance problem you tackled and the technical choice you made.

cards.where: Senior Software Engineer, Payments Platform, line 5
cards.line: Mentor two mid-level engineers through code review and design docs
cards.cannot_tell: For a management role, decisions about team direction or engineer development would add to the mentoring shown here.
cards.example: Mentor two mid-level engineers through code review and design docs; [team direction or development decision you made]
cards.question: What decisions have you made about the team's direction or the engineers' development?

cards.where: Senior Software Engineer, Payments Platform, line 4
cards.line: Wrote the on-call runbooks for the payments services and ran the incident reviews for the platform group
cards.cannot_tell: A change that came from an incident review could show how you improved platform operations.
cards.example: Wrote the on-call runbooks for the payments services and ran the incident reviews for the platform group; [operational change from an incident review]
cards.question: What operational change, if any, came from an incident review you ran?

fit.why: Your headline and latest role center on backend payments systems, from payouts and the ledger to API performance.
fit.level: senior, leads technical projects and mentors two engineers
fit.note: Your on-call runbooks and incident reviews also connect to the operational side of the Cobalt Pay role. If you've set delivery priorities with Product or worked with Finance, Risk or Support, make that work visible.

posting.summary: Cobalt Pay seeks an engineering manager to lead a payments platform team owning payouts and the ledger.
missing: 2+ years managing engineers with direct reports, including hiring and performance management
Experience leading teams that run production systems with on-call
A record of growing engineers into senior roles

covered.requirement: 5+ years of backend engineering before moving into management
covered.line: Designed and built the idempotent payouts service in Go and PostgreSQL that now settles about 1.8M payouts a month
